ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant KYC/EDD protocols: screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized agents against Canadian sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 31), UN Security Council sanctions implemented under the United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2, and OFAC SDN/Consolidated lists as secondary business risk; PEP determination for domestic, foreign and international-organization PEPs, including family members and close associates; enhanced due diligence is mandatory because the platform is a money-services business under the PCMLTFA Part 1 and the Quebec Money-Services Businesses Act; mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC and record-keeping per SOR/2002-184.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; required NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) obtained via a REQ-licensed search house.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), a Quebec enterprise name must be in French; a bilingual name is accepted only if French is equally or more prominent; names must use Latin script and may not contain numerals, punctuation or symbols not accepted by REQ; non-French tokens (e.g., 'Lending', 'Pay') require French equivalents or a recognized exception; every name must include a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'Société par actions'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Filing instructions: submit an application for name reservation to REQ together with a current NUANS report; upon rejection, the applicant may (1) file a written review request with the registrar under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1) within 30 days of the decision, providing justifications and supporting evidence, and (2) on a final refusal, appeal to the Court of Québec (Cour du Québec) within 30 days of the review decision; alternatively, the applicant may file a revised reservation request with a new name and an updated NUANS report; reservation fees are non-refundable in all cases.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for a licensed Quebec money-services business: authorization under the Money-Services Businesses Act (CQLR c S-29.01) requires a physical establishment in Quebec, local recordkeeping, and a person responsible accessible during business hours; at the pure incorporation stage a virtual or registered-agent address may be used only temporarily, but it must be replaced by a physical office before AMF authorization and FINTRAC MSB registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (>85%) – FINTRAC risk-based examinations and AMF unannounced on-site inspections are prioritized for digital lending and money-services businesses; P2P micro-lending with algorithmic underwriting is flagged as a high-risk, high-volume sector requiring on-site verification of records, IT systems and customer due diligence files.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 7-20 (incorporation), s. 24 (by-laws), ss. 84-85 (registered office), ss. 122-123 (directors duties); Code civil du Quebec arts. 298-309
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Business Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; incorporation may proceed with nominal capital. Articles must declare authorized share capital; any issued shares must be fully paid for in money, property, or past services. No escrow bank account is required; client funds, if any, must be segregated in trust per Quebec consumer protection rules before lending activities begin.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Articles of Incorporation submitted to the Registraire des entreprises be adopted; the registered office shall be at [street address, city, Quebec]; the following individuals are appointed directors for the first term: [Name], [Name], [Name]; the corporate seal is adopted; the initial by-laws are ratified; shares are issued to subscribers in accordance with the subscription agreement; officers are elected as President, Secretary, and Treasurer; and management is authorized to open bank accounts, complete regulatory filings, and pay incorporation costs. Further resolved that no director or officer may transact related-party loans without full board approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (online portal of the Quebec enterprise registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Quebec enterprise registry (REQ) to confirm the proposed corporate name is distinct and compliant. Submit the applicable name declaration or reservation request through the online platform and obtain the certificate of name reservation.
required_dossiers: Combined name declaration/declaration de designation, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, modify the distinctive element or legal suffix (e.g., Inc., Corp.) and file a revised name declaration electronically; the registry fee is reapplied only if the previous application was incomplete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Registration Statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (online filing and in-person counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the statuts de constitution (Articles of Incorporation) online, including authorized share structure, initial directors and their addresses, and the first registered office. Pay the statutory filing fee by secure electronic transfer. Receive the Certificate of Incorporation and the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) once the record is accepted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried for deficiency, correct the deficiency online under the same application number. Any material defect that changes the corporate name or share structure requires a new filing and fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of By-laws and Appointment of Initial Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Shareholders acting at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or execute a written resolution. Adopt the initial by-laws, confirm the registered office, appoint directors, elect officers, approve the share subscription agreements, and authorize the dropping of the corporate seal. Record resolutions and consents in the corporate records book.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice for organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any irregularity in the organizational process is cured by a supplemental written resolution of the board of directors; where the registry requires the filing of by-laws, submit within 15 days of adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Completion of Corporate Governance Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass the formal first board resolution confirming the share subscription, registered office, selection of officers, banking resolutions, financial year-end, and auditor designation. Compile and maintain the securities register, directors register, and statutory minute book in accordance with the Business Corporations Act (Quebec).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies in the corporate record are rectified by a unanimous written consent of directors and, if necessary, a corrective resolution addressing the share issuance or officer appointment before the first financial statements are prepared.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html (federal TIN, GST/HST, payroll and corporate income tax); Revenu Québec at https://www.revenuquebec.ca (Quebec Sales Tax / TVQ, QPIP payroll and Quebec corporation tax). The federal Business Number (BN) is the primary TIN and the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) is the provincial identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated fintech applying to operate in Quebec must (1) obtain a 9-digit Business Number from the CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1, opening program accounts RP0001 (GST/HST), RC0001 (corporate income tax) and RP0001 (payroll) as applicable; (2) file Form RC2401 (Application for a Determination of Residency of a Corporation) with certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, articles of continuance and a foreign tax residency certificate if the entity is non-resident; (3) complete extra-provincial registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) and apply to Revenu Québec on the combined registration form (demande d'inscription) to obtain the NEQ and QST/TVQ accounts; (4) where a US parent or member is present, file Form RC4145 (Election for Treaty Benefits) to trigger the Canada-US Article IV(7) fiscally-transparent entity election. Processing times are approximately 2-8 weeks federally and 10-15 business days provincially.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian Business Corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a resident taxpayer subject to the Income Tax Act with worldwide income and a separate legal personality; no pass-through election exists. Because non-resident ownership is present, the entity is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), so the small business deduction is unavailable; the general combined federal and Quebec corporate rate is 26.5% (15% federal plus 11.5% Quebec). Taxation is residence-based, not strictly territorial, with foreign tax credits mitigating double taxation. For GST/HST/QST, the entity will be a financial institution engaged in lending, making its core interest and fee income exempt supplies; it is not automatically a selected listed financial institution unless statutory thresholds are met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box regime; however, the following elections and mandatory anti-hybrid settings apply: (i) Canada-US Tax Treaty Article IV(7) election via Form RC4145 that deems a US fiscally-transparent entity to be a resident of the US for treaty benefits; (ii) domestic hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.3, 18.4, 19.2, 20.2, 21.2 and 247.1) operate non-electively to disallow double deductions and deduction/non-inclusion outcomes; (iii) GST/HST elections include the ETA s. 156 related-party election, the closely related corporation election, the GST/HST Quick Method election, and the annual filing election; (iv) for Quebec, parallel elections are available under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c T-2.1); (v) Part XIV branch tax elections under ITA s. 219 do not normally apply once the Canadian entity is a separate resident corporation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority; prudential supervision of federally regulated deposit-taking institutions is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing supervision is exercised by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). In Quebec, the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) licenses money-services businesses under the Act respecting money-services businesses (CQLR c S-41.1), and the Office de la protection du consommateur (OPC) issues permits for consumer lending activities under the Consumer Protection Act (Québec).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is free-floating and fully convertible. Canada repealed its exchange-control legislation in 1951 and currently imposes no restrictions, pre-approvals, or quota systems on current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit and capital remittances (dividends, interest, royalties, loan repayments, liquidation proceeds) may flow freely, subject to statutory withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) — generally 25% on dividends and interest paid to non-residents, treaty-reduced where applicable — and to FATCA/CRS reporting. FINTRAC reporting thresholds (cross-border electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more) are informational AML/ATF obligations and do not constitute a convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory rule requiring surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation of export proceeds or foreign-currency receivables to the Bank of Canada or any licensed intermediary. A Canadian-domiciled P2P micro-lending platform may hold and reinvest foreign-currency operational balances abroad, subject to the functional-currency rules of section 261 of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and to FINTRAC's cross-border EFT reporting duty for transactions of CAD 10,000 or more, which must be reported within five business days.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as principal treasury and clearing rail; MEDIUM as an ancillary disbursement channel only. Canada does not recognize the European EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licence. An offshore EMI operating in Canada must register with FINTRAC as a money-services business (MSB) and, if active in Quebec, hold an AMF money-services business licence. Foreign EMIs cannot become direct participants in Payments Canada's ACSS or Lynx, cannot originate Pre-Authorized Debits, and do not provide CDIC deposit insurance or client-fund custody arrangements acceptable to Quebec financial regulators. The platform should therefore maintain its primary CAD liquidity and settlement accounts exclusively at a Canadian Schedule I bank or a Quebec-based cooperative institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) that directors appear physically for corporate account opening; FINTRAC permits remote identification under the G7 identification method and video-based KYC. However, for a High_Risk_Special_License P2P lending platform, tier-1 Canadian banks will in practice contractually mandate a physical board/mandate meeting at the bank's Commercial Banking Centre in Montreal, plus an in-person interview with the platform's designated Anti-Money-Laundering Officer and Compliance Officer. Remote small-account opening is not viable until the banking relationship matures, typically after a 12-month operating track record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Platform classified as a high-risk money-services business operating pooled client funds and settlement accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC MSB registration confirmation; AMF money-services business licence issued to the Quebec entity; written AML/ATF compliance programme covering policies, risk assessment, training, compliance officer and independent annual review; executed client-funds trust deed and bank undertaking controlling the pooled settlement account; third-party audit letter confirming adequacy of the transaction monitoring system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership concentration or opacity in the shareholder structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec Register of Enterprises (Registraire des entreprises) beneficial-ownership certification under the Act respecting the transparency of enterprises; CBCA/QBCA share register and directors' resolution; certified passports and proof-of-address for each ultimate beneficial owner above 25%; tax residency certificates for each UBO; source-of-wealth statement signed by each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Criminal-rate exposure under section 347 of the Criminal Code (Canada) and Quebec Consumer Protection Act sub-prime lending caps
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion issued by a member of the Quebec bar confirming that the algorithmically determined effective annual rate is capped below 35% APR for loans under CAD 10,000 as required by the Regulation under the Consumer Protection Act (Québec) and below the 60% criminal rate threshold; current rate methodology disclosure document; example amortization schedules including all-in costs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Repeat small-dollar transaction flows deemed atypical for a micro-lending platform (potential money laundering through repayment cycles)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC-compliant suspicious-transaction-reporting framework; real-time transaction-monitoring and anomaly-detection engine logs; borrower-lender reconstruction algorithms and reconciliation reports; large-cash and large cross-border EFT reporting procedures for CAD 10,000 or more; designated compliance officer certification of the STR escalation workflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, terrorist-financing and politically exposed person (PEP) concerns arising from the bank's sanctions screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive automated sanctions-screening solution covering all borrowers, lenders, UBOs and counterparties; legal opinion on compliance with the Special Economic Measures Act (Canada) and United Nations Act; OFSI/OSFI due-diligence certificate; negative PEP registration for all directors; audit log of screening false-positive reviews.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No exchange-control authorization is required. Equity injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's bank with an unambiguous reference (e.g., Share subscription, corporate resolution dated, file no. at the Registraire des entreprises) into the National Bank of Canada operational account, settling in CAD over Lynx (Canada's high-value settlement system) for same-day credit. Shareholder loans must be supported by an executed facility agreement, board resolution, and CRS/FATCA self-certifications; contractual interest must be at arm's length to avoid Part XIII withholding (25% statutory, treaty-reduced) and Quebec tax filing obligations. All inbound cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC within five business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic disbursement of micro-loans will be executed through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) operated by Payments Canada, using Pre-Authorized Debits (PAD) for collections and PAD credits/direct deposits for disbursements. Local wallet payouts will use Interac e-Transfer and Visa Direct / Mastercard Send APIs integrated through the bank's open-banking gateway. Cross-border vendor and licensing disbursements will clear by SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank cover) through the sponsoring bank's correspondent network, with the CAD leg settling over Lynx. Commercial letters of credit remain permissible under Canadian law and are reserved for platform procurement of infrastructure services; they are not suitable for micro-lending payout flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) documented under an ISDA 1992 or 2002 Master Agreement with an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) to align platform borrowing and lending currency liabilities
Plain-vanilla FX options (European-style call/put) and zero-cost collars for budget-rate protection
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) covering non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies when the platform extends cross-border loan receivable exposures
Exchange-traded FX futures and options listed on the Montréal Exchange / CME for margin-efficient micro-hedging, subject to board-approved derivative-use limits and an OSFI-compliant hedge policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal annual return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada — Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the corporation's incorporation, filed every calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a Corporations Canada late-filing charge; failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution after prior notice; revival requires filing of overdue returns and payment of applicable fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual update declaration (déclaration annuelle de mise à jour)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the month following the anniversary of the corporation's registration in the Quebec enterprise register, filed every calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file after successive annual notices permits administrative dissolution or striking-off by the Registraire des entreprises; overdue filers must pay late fees and may require restoration or reactivation procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year end, filed annually; for a December 31 fiscal end the due date is June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months; repeated habitual failure may increase penalty to 10% plus 2% per month; interest compounds on unpaid balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year end, filed annually; for a December 31 fiscal end the due date is June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month under the Taxation Act; repeated failure may increase penalty rates; interest is compounded daily on unpaid taxes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No fixed statutory size threshold under CBCA/QBCA for a non-distributing private corporation; an independent auditor can be waived by unanimous shareholder consent or the consent of holders of not less than 95% of votes. Compulsory audit is triggered if the corporation is a distributing corporation, if the regulator requires an audit as a money-lending permit or AML/ATF licensing condition, or if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares apply for an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook; Part I IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Part II Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private corporations; CRA and Revenu Québec accept statutorily compliant financial statements under these frameworks.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The corporation must maintain and update its internal register of individuals with significant control (ISC) after any share transfer or change in control; holders owning 25% or more of issued shares or exercising de facto control must be identified. Federal CBCA corporations must report ISC information to Corporations Canada with the annual return; Quebec corporations must confirm ultimate beneficial ownership information in the annual update declaration filed with the Registraire des entreprises.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
